definitions.explanation: Two or more people having or wearing the same design of item, deliberately matched. Most often used of clothes or accessories.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦カップ→カップ：01077_kappu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{夫婦|ふうふ}→夫婦：03592_fuufu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧お{揃|そろ}いだ。
examples.english: These cups are a matching pair for the couple.

examples.japanese: ⟦{友達|ともだち}→友達：01478_tomodachi⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{旅行|りょこう}→旅行：00748_ryokou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{記念|きねん}→記念：00232_kinen⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧お{揃|そろ}い⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦キー→キー：10869_kii⟧ホルダー⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}った→買う：00489_kau⟧。
examples.english: My friend and I bought matching keychains as a souvenir of the trip.

notes:
From ⟦{揃|そろ}う→揃う：01953_sorou⟧ (to match, to be complete) with the polite prefix お〜. Refers to people deliberately having the same item, usually with a friendly or affectionate nuance.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{揃|そろ}い⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{服|ふく}→服：00695_fuku⟧: matching outfits
- お{揃|そろ}い⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to make (items) matching
- ⟦ペア→ペア：11265_pea⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧お{揃|そろ}い: a matching pair

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ペアルック: matching couple's outfits — loanword, specifically for couples dressing alike
- ⟦{同|おな}じ→同じ：02857_onaji⟧: the same — plain factual sameness, without the coordinated, intentional nuance

cross_references.label: to be complete, to be uniform
